text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The monthly water bill for all households will be more than doubled by the year 2000 under new pricing structure announced by the government to ensure Singaporeans never go thirsty.
- Singapore-Philippine relations reach new heights with leaders from both countries agreeing to develop blueprint to foster closer cooperation in future.
- Singapore Telecom (SingTel) is planning to take "significant equity stakes" in major telecommunications operators in Thailand and Indonesia.

- United States will declare in two months lowered rates it is attempting to force on overseas telephone carriers for completing connection of international calls made from its jurisdication, US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) commissioner says.
- Thailand, struggling to safeguard its currency, has tightened controls on moving money into and out of country.

- Top Asian telecom and multimedia players, led by Japanese powerhouse Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT), launch grouping that could usher in new era in regional cooperation in fast-growing area of multimedia.
- Upward trend in COE premiums this year has continued, with tender for July certificates of entitlement to own cars resulting in prices rising as much as Singapore $6,600 or 10 percent.

- Mainboard-listed Thakral Corp Ltd (TCL) turns in better-than-expected 20 percent jump in net profit to Singapore $68.6 million for fiscal year ended March, even though turnover rose only marginally.
- Californian court rules Creative Technology cannot prevent the use of a Windows 95 audio driver in computer systems based at Cyrix's MediaGX processor.
- DBS Land shares close at six-month low of Singapore $4.56, down eight cents, after slipping as low as Singapore $4.46 in intra-day trading.
- Blue-chip food company Cerebos Pacific Ltd dashes market hopes of double-digit growth in earnings, with an unchanged operating outcome at halfway mark and warning of tougher second half.
- First Capital Corp (FCC) teams up with Indonesian heavy-weights to develop prime Jakarta site.
- Small investors will receive just under half telephone cord maker Huan Hsin's eight million initial public offer shares available to the public.
